name: danwagnerco/similarweb
what_it_holds: Python client wrapping the official SimilarWeb API (traffic/engagement endpoints: visits, page views, bounce rate, traffic sources, by domain). No data committed; every call requires a paid SimilarWeb API key (free trial only, rate-limited).
why_useful: SimilarWeb-style web-traffic estimates for airbnb.com are named explicitly in gap 5 as a target category; this is the best-maintained (51-star, MIT) open client for that API, useful IF the team ever obtains a SimilarWeb trial key, but yields nothing without one.
themes: Alternative-data vendor sample repos: vendors publishing free samples on GitHub (Advan, Similarweb, Apptopia, Yipit-like, Consumer Edge, Earnest, M Science, Quiver Quant, Thinknum)
why_all: SimilarWeb-style web-traffic estimates for airbnb.com are named explicitly in gap 5 as a target category; this is the best-maintained (51-star, MIT) open client for that API, useful IF the team ever obtains a SimilarWeb trial key, but yields nothing without one.
Backup client if the free-API approach above breaks; requires a paid Similarweb key so lower priority than the free-endpoint repo.

name: goiener-smartmeter-mirror
what_it_holds: Mirror of the GoiEner smart-meter dataset (original: Universidad de Deusto / GoiEner, Zenodo, CC-BY 4.0): raw.tzst (2.0GB compressed, ~15GB unpacked) containing 25,559 per-supply-point CSV files of hourly household electricity consumption (kWh) for the Basque Country / Navarre region of Spain, 2014-11-02 to 2022-06-08, plus metadata.csv (tariffs, contracted power, location). Committed as actual data, not a link; downloaded/re-hosted 2026-09-13, unmodified, with attribution.
why_useful: A genuine open, granular (hourly, per-meter, ~8 year span) smart-meter electricity panel — exactly the modality this theme is scouting for as an occupancy/activity proxy, even though the geography (Basque/Navarre, mixed residential) is not purely touristic; usable as a template/comparator for building an ADR-orthogonal occupancy proxy or for testing the smart-meter-as-occupancy-proxy method before looking for a tourist-specific panel.
license: CC-BY 4.0 (per repo note; possible CC-BY-SA ambiguity per upstream Zenodo record)
themes: Electricity, water and waste data as occupancy proxies (smart-meter open data, tourist-area utility consumption), and mobile-phone tourism statistics (Eurostat MNO experimental)
why_all: A genuine open, granular (hourly, per-meter, ~8 year span) smart-meter electricity panel — exactly the modality this theme is scouting for as an occupancy/activity proxy, even though the geography (Basque/Navarre, mixed residential) is not purely touristic; usable as a template/comparator for building an ADR-orthogonal occupancy proxy or for testing the smart-meter-as-occupancy-proxy method before looking for a tourist-specific panel.

name: eCommerce-dataset-samples
what_it_holds: Bright Data (formerly Luminati) org repo of committed sample datasets, one per retailer, each >1,000 records, in JSON/NDJSON/CSV/Parquet (optionally gzipped). Sites covered: Amazon, Walmart, Target, eBay, Zara, Home Depot, plus more. Fields (~17 per record): title, ASIN/product id, URL, initial_price, final_price, currency, availability/inventory, reviews_count, rating, description, categories, brand, features, images_count, image_url, seller info, delivery details. Described as subsets of larger paid datasets with 'millions of records'; no dates/geography stated in README, 91 stars, updated 13 Sep 2026 (actively maintained).
why_useful: Directly the requested template: a real, committed multi-retailer price/rank/review-count dataset schema (price, rating, review velocity, availability) that is the closest open analogue to what a scraped Airbnb search-page panel would need to look like for point-in-time price/availability nowcasting. Useful as a schema/format reference for the team's own fee-panel search-page capture (rule #6) and for gap #2 (realised price/occupancy proxies) methodology, even though it is retail not travel.
size_hint: >1,000 records per sample file across ~6+ retailers; full paid dataset described as millions of rows
geography: not stated (likely US-centric given US retailers listed)
themes: Retail and ecommerce alt-data open samples (web-scraped prices, Amazon rank), as templates for platform KPI nowcasting
why_all: Directly the requested template: a real, committed multi-retailer price/rank/review-count dataset schema (price, rating, review velocity, availability) that is the closest open analogue to what a scraped Airbnb search-page panel would need to look like for point-in-time price/availability nowcasting. Useful as a schema/format reference for the team's own fee-panel search-page capture (rule #6) and for gap #2 (realised price/occupancy proxies) methodology, even though it is retail not travel.

name: ashermanwmf/pageviewapi
what_it_holds: Small client/wrapper for Wikimedia's official Pageviews API, returning per-article, per-day pageview counts back to mid-2015.
why_useful: Matches CONTEXT gap #5 ('Wikipedia pageviews tooling') directly; Wikipedia pageviews for 'Airbnb', 'short-term rental', competitor articles, or destination-city articles are a free, long-history, point-in-time-clean (pageviews are immutable once logged) engagement/interest proxy that has not been tested by the team yet.
size_hint: client only, API pull required for data
last_activity: check repo (appears stale; the canonical/actively-maintained alternative is Wikimedia's own `wikimedia/mediawiki-services-pageview-api` or the `mwviews`/`pageviewapi` PyPI package — flag for a follow-up scout to find the best-maintained client)

name: rohitgodbole/WikiPageviews
what_it_holds: A thin wrapper (0 stars) around the official Wikimedia Pageviews API, updated as recently as 26 Apr 2026.
why_useful: CONTEXT gap #5 flags 'Wikipedia pageviews tooling' explicitly; pageviews for 'Airbnb', 'Vrbo', destination-city pages, or 'short-term rental' articles are free, dated-by-day, genuinely point-in-time (the API returns historical daily counts as originally recorded) and could proxy search/engagement interest as an alternative to non-point-in-time Google Trends. The official Wikimedia REST pageviews API itself (no wrapper needed) is the more load-bearing artifact here; this repo is just one thin client example.
time_coverage: Wikimedia pageviews API covers July 2015-present daily/hourly, official and point-in-time
